_about: The first night (docs/vision/vertical-slice.md beat 8; game-design.md 7.6 on claude-a/game-design-v2): the first prepared raid on Crossroads. core/raids.gd reads it. Positions are world px local to the zone, as in data/plans/crossroads.json; the lane and the gate pad are the plan's own (looked up by id). Every number marked placeholder is one to tune in play-tests; none is balanced. The purse is in data/balance/glint.json (raids.first_night).
title: The first night
why_announce_if: the raid comes from the lantern's light (attention), and is announced only once the homecoming quest is over, so beat 8 follows beat 7 (a decision for Matt)
why_lane_points: the plan's halt_road to the square's edge, then round the south of the well (its solid 278-298 x 304-320) to the south-west of the shard lantern's plinth (344-360 x 314-320; 13 Nov: the lantern moved off the well's ring to the east of the gate walk). The strike spot (338, 326) stands in front of both pictures (the well's sorts at y 320 and spans x 269-307, the lantern's sorts at 320 and spans x 343-361), so the raider is not hidden behind the well's frame or the lantern (audit of #483, B2 and P1). The plan's halt_road lane now holds the same points; test_raids.gd holds that a creature's body fits along the whole lane

pads.why: inside the street between the bakery (foot at y 288) and the herbalist's (top at y 336): its span closes the street wall to wall, so the halt road is shut until it breaks

the street's mouth onto the square, the same span from wall to wall. Replaces the plan's pad_halt_gate (210, 300), which stands in the open square where a hurdle can be walked round (audit of #483, B1). Where the pads go is Matt's open decision (vertical-slice.md, Open for Matt 6): move them here, in the raid's data

hurdle_barricade.name: Hurdle barricade
hurdle_barricade.text: Blocks the road until it is broken
hurdle_barricade.why_span: world px across the lane when a pad gives no span of its own

lantern.why: a raider strikes the lantern only standing within `reach` world px of its plinth (`box`, the lit lantern's solid in zones/crossroads/kit.json); `foot` is the plinth's foot, where its health and its struck light are drawn from
lantern.why_dark: the stake (Matt, 13 Nov: "Shard dims until held"): a lost night sets the save flag `dark_flag` and only a won night clears it (core/raids.gd). While it is set, world/raid_night.gd lays the struck glass's dark pane over `picture`, the zone's lit lantern (a Sprite2D whose position is the plinth's foot), and the lantern pools no light when a wave comes. `unlit` is the zone's unlit lantern picture (the same size and foot as the lit one) and `unlit_parts` the rectangles of it, in picture px, drawn over the lit picture outside the glass: every pixel where the two pictures differ outside the pane (the glass's two posts, x 16 and 49; the sill, y 120; the line of light down the pedestal, y 124 to 155). The glass itself keeps the lit picture under the dark pane, so the shard is still seen in its cradle. The `repairs` below show for as long. No Glint, quest or restore is taken

signal.text: Three blows from the forge: the night has begun.
signal.why: night one is called by Hale at her anvil, not by a bell (Matt, 13 Nov; the bell tower is rebuilt later and rung for the wolf moon). The cue is `raid_anvil` (core/raids.gd ring). `anvil` is the zone's anvil, shown only while the forge is restored; `at` (world px) is its face, where world/raid_signal.gd throws a spark for each of the cue's three blows. `card` and `text` are the card that says so wherever the player stands

why_notice: world px: nearer than this, with nothing solid between, a marching creature turns on the player (the camps notice at 100; a raider keeps to its road longer)

first_wave.why: wave 1 waits for the player to come within `within` world px of the plan's place `near` (the square), or `or_after` seconds, and never comes sooner than `at_least`: the anvil is sounded on the screen where the player walked in (the garden walk, about 20 s from the square), and two boarlets break a hurdle in about 8 s (audit round 2, R2-2). Not a combat number

waves.why: two boarlets: the hurdles take the first knocks
a toad that spits over the hurdle at the archer
a mossback and the horned elite last

repairs.why: rough planks nailed over the smithy's front window (smithy.png, right of the forge mouth) after the lost night. `at` is a point on the window: scripts/art/native/town.py finds the opening of the building `over` under it and draws the planks in that building's own frame, so they sit on its frame exactly (village.p_window_boards_hd). `foot` sorts it in front of the building. No solid: it is on the wall

the square's handcart, wrecked by the raiders and tipped back on its tail, its wheel knocked off (village.p_cart_wreck_hd), south of the halt road's lane where it comes onto the square, where the storm rubble `square_rubble_a` stood (220-250 x 340-358, solid until the shard came home). `solid` is its bed on the setts (world px; world/raid_repair.gd puts it on the walls' layer, and on the low layer only when its picture stands under tools/gen_physics.py's LOW_RISE: the picture is 75 texels tall and stands 65 above its foot, at or over LOW_RISE 64, so it stops shots too; test_raids.gd holds that): the lane passes 11.5 px north of its north-east corner (248, 336) and 23 px from its north-west one, Morel's spot (200, 352) is 25 px from it, the herbalist's (to x 184) 40 px west and the bench under the well (276-300 x 362-368) 28 px east; its foot (236, 344) is on the soft grid (x on a half cell, y on a cell line). test_raids.gd holds that every route still walks with it

offers.name: The library's bell tower
offers.why_mark: a restore mark in front of the library's door (248, 200), set out by world/raid_night.gd once the raid is won and the bell tower not yet restored; the plan holds no site for it yet
offers.why: the bell tower (game-design.md 7.2, the library's cupola; act 1's restore id bell_tower at the 50 Glint its mark's lines quote, docs/story/act1.md) is offered for stage 1. core/raids.gd adds it to Village.sites only while no plan defines bell_tower; its picture arrives with stage 1's art; its mark is set out by world/raid_night.gd (`mark`). Hale no longer speaks of it (Matt, 13 Nov: she says the night was a one-off; data/dialogue/raids.json)
